chunks: Aban narrated from Abū al-ʿAbbās, meaning al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله declare al-Madīnah a sanctuary?" He said: "Yes, he declared a barīd by a barīd as sacred, [regarding] its ʿiḍāhā."
I said: "Its game?" He said: "The people do not lie."

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةَ: Madinah, the city discussed as a sanctuary
key_terms.بَرِيداً: a measured distance used to define the sanctuary boundary
key_terms.صَيْدَهَا: the game animals of the sanctuary area
key_terms.عِضَاهَا: its thorny trees or natural vegetation
key_terms.لَا يَكْذِبُ النَّاسُ: an affirmation that the people’s report on this matter is not false

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله make Madinah a sanctuary, and what did that include?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله designated al-Madīnah as a sacred precinct within a measured boundary. It indicates legal sanctity attached to the area, especially concerning its vegetation, and alludes to the known ruling regarding its hunting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3154 - Aban narrated from Abu al-‘Abbas, meaning al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), "Did the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) declare Medina a sanctuary?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, he declared an area of a barid (about 22 kilometers) by a barid as a sanctuary, forbidding the cutting of its of its ʿIdhāhāʾ (trees)."

I then asked: "What about its hunting?"
Imam (as) replied: "People do not lie."
